---
title: "Demo gallery"
description: "Working maps and networks, with standalone HTML downloads and reproducible R scripts."
output: html_document
---

Explore an example, download its standalone HTML, or use its R script as a
starting point for your own data. Every live demo below runs entirely in your
browser. Downloaded HTML files work without R, a server, or an internet connection.

The images are static ggplot2 previews. Interactive viewers have their own
controls and presentation. On a small screen, opening the demo directly gives
it more room than an embedded frame.

## Run an example yourself

Install offlineatlas, then run an example script in a dedicated output folder.
The scripts use bundled data and replace their previous example exports.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(offlineatlas)
dir.create("atlas-examples", showWarnings = FALSE)
setwd("atlas-examples")
source(system.file("examples", "gdp.R", package = "offlineatlas"))
browseURL("world-bank-gdp.html")
```

Each **R code** link above opens the complete script. The scripts are also
installed with the package. For publication figures, see the
[static map script](../examples/static.R) and
[static network script](../examples/static_networks.R). Their PNG, PDF, and SVG
outputs can be recreated locally. For example, compare the
[automatic network PNG](../images/florence_automatic.png) with its
[vector PDF](../images/florence_automatic.pdf).

The [tutorial](getting-started.html) explains how to adapt these examples.
The [function reference](../reference/index.html) describes the available options.

## A living example on the web

[FDI Atlas](https://fdiatlas.engagedthinking.com/) is a related, more customized
project. It shows how an atlas can become a public resource. For the standalone
package exports, publishing can be as simple as putting the HTML file on a
website. Everything embedded in that file is available to its viewers.

Full source notes and data reuse terms appear inside the exported viewers and
in the package’s bundled notices. Downloaded demos retain those notices.
